html:
SMTO-GML-0064 — This filter can't be applied to emails you already have

GUID: a3bbc38a-29c8-4f3c-9a2e-5376c3f261b3
Slug: gmail-filter-retroactive-unsupported
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail-client-actions

What happened

  • SMTO can apply a filter to emails you already have only if it matches simple things like sender or subject and only changes labels. This filter forwards mail, uses an unsupported condition, or has conflicting label changes. Nothing was created or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to apply only label changes to existing emails, such as adding a label, archiving or marking as read, and leave forwarding out. Old emails can't be forwarded by a filter, so SMTO refuses rather than pretending it did.
  2. Use simple conditions: from, to, subject, words to include or leave out, has attachment, or size larger or smaller than an amount. Don't put quote marks in the from, to or subject text. SMTO turns these conditions into a Gmail search, and other conditions or quote marks can't be searched for reliably.
  3. Don't add or remove the Sent or Drafts labels, and don't add and remove the same label in one filter. Those label changes aren't allowed on existing emails or contradict each other.
  4. If you want forwarding, ask SMTO to create the filter for new emails only, without applying it to existing ones. Forwarding only works as mail arrives, so it belongs in a filter for future emails.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows how many existing emails the filter matches and applies the label changes, or creates the filter for new mail only.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to forward old emails one by one to imitate the filter.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Retroactive filter preparation rejected the criteria or action: forwarding, a non-queryable criterion (such as excludeChats), quotes or newlines in from/to/subject, size without sizeComparison, DRAFT or SENT label effects, or empty or conflicting label changes.

What this means

  • Retroactive filter preparation accepts queryable predicates and permitted label effects. Forwarding, unsupported criteria, draft/sent label assignments and conflicting label changes are rejected before creation or mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Retroactive filter preparation accepts queryable predicates and permitted label effects. Forwarding, unsupported criteria, draft/sent label assignments and conflicting label changes are rejected before creation or mutation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected account, action arguments and operation reference; do not infer mailbox effects from the error alone.

How to fix it

  • Restrict apply_filter and create_filter_and_apply to queryable criteria (from, to, subject, query, negatedQuery, hasAttachment, size with sizeComparison) and nonconflicting addLabelIds/removeLabelIds that exclude DRAFT and SENT. Use plain filter creation for delivery-time effects such as forwarding; filter_spec in gmail/client_actions rejects before any filter is created or mail changes.
  • Choose equivalent mailbox actions or edit the retroactive request to supported criteria and label changes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Choose equivalent mailbox actions or edit the retroactive request to supported criteria and label changes.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported effects are validated before a filter is created or existing mail changes.

What not to do

  • Do not forward old messages or imitate delivery-time settings while claiming to apply a filter.

Technical notes

  • This check rejects new work before its write. It does not undo previous confirmed effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
